newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FDA approves new osteoporosis test device.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FDA approves new osteoporosis test device.

text.p: A U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) panel has advised approval of a new ultrasound device that should make it easier to test for osteoporosis.
Hologic Inc.'s Sahara device uses ultrasound to test the density of the heel bone. This should tell doctors whether someone is at risk of the disease, which weakens bones.

Hologic says Sahara is as clinically useful and cheaper, safer and more accessible than the usual method now used -- dual X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). But the panel, whose advice the FDA usually follows, said Sahara could only be used to "predict" results of DXA, which may curb enthusiasm for the device.
Hologic says Sahara, which weighs 20 pounds (10 kg) and costs $30,000, may increase access to screening and therefore mean more sufferers will be treated.

The FDA panel said on Monday that Hologic needed to include more information in its labeling on usage by men and non-white females, and better physician and patient education about when to use the device.
Osteoporosis affects more than 20 million women and 1.5 million men in the United States alone, and up to three million people in Britain.
